about: Accepted high and critical npm advisories in mobile's shipped dependency tree (npm audit --omit=dev).
Read by infra/scripts/check-npm-audit.py in the mobile CI job. An advisory not listed here fails CI,
and every entry fails CI from its expires date (UTC), so each one is re-reviewed rather than forgotten.
2026-10-03: 71 advisories in 20 packages. 2026-10-04: a lockfile-only update (npm update of the advisory
packages; no package.json change) fixed 62 of them without moving any native module. npm audit fix fixed
fewer and moved 12 native modules (expo 54.0.30 to 54.0.37, expo-updates, expo-notifications, expo-modules-core
and others), which would need a new App Store binary. The 9 left need an Expo SDK major (image-size, postcss),
an aws-amplify bump that changes bundled sign-in code (fast-xml-parser), or an upstream release that does not
exist yet (node-forge, braces); each reason says which. Delete an entry when npm stops reporting it.
evidence: 2026-10-04, mobile @ origin/main ebc2c10 plus the 2026-10-04 lockfile, npm 11.6.0: npm audit --omit=dev flagged
58 packages, most only because they depend on another one; underneath are 9 high or critical advisories in 5
packages (below). npx expo export --platform ios --platform android --source-maps bundled 146 packages, and none
of the 5 is among them. Re-check a reason with that export and the .hbc.map sources.
The 2026-10-04 lockfile changed three bundled packages (nanoid 3.3.11 to 3.3.19, uuid 11.1.0 to 11.1.1, hasown
2.0.2 to 2.0.4); no package entered or left the bundle, and an unminified export differs only in nanoid's
non-secure loop guard, uuid's buffer bounds check and the Sentry debug id. expo-modules-autolinking resolve and
react-native-config output (iOS and Android) is identical before and after.

entries.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
entries.reason: Not in the shipped app: absent from the iOS and Android Metro source maps (see evidence). Build-time only: expo > metro-file-map > micromatch glob matching in Metro, on repo-controlled patterns. No fixed release: the advisory covers <=3.0.3 and 3.0.3 is the newest braces; it leaves the tree only when Metro stops using micromatch (npm proposes react-native 0.87.1, a major).

entries.title: fast-xml-parser affected by numeric entity expansion bypassing all entity expansion limits (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-26278)
entries.reason: Not in the shipped app: absent from the iOS and Android Metro source maps (see evidence). aws-amplify > @aws-amplify/analytics > @aws-sdk/client-firehose, client-kinesis and client-personalize-events > @aws-sdk/core 3.621.0, which pins fast-xml-parser 4.4.1 exactly; the app imports only aws-amplify/auth. The top-level copy (4.5.7, @aws-amplify/storage) is already fixed. The fix is lockfile-only (npm update aws-amplify: 6.15.9 to 6.22.1), but it also changes bundled sign-in code (@aws-amplify/auth 6.17.1 to 6.21.1, @aws-amplify/core 6.15.0 to 6.19.2), so it is left for its own OTA after a sign-in test on a device.

entries.title: image-size: JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
entries.reason: Not in the shipped app: absent from the iOS and Android Metro source maps (see evidence). Build-time only: expo > metro reads the dimensions of the repo's own image assets. No lockfile fix: every metro 0.83.x (Expo SDK 54, through @expo/metro 54.2.0) requires image-size ^1.0.2, and 1.2.1, the newest 1.x, is affected (both advisories end at 2.0.2). It leaves with the Expo SDK major that moves Metro.

entries.title: node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements
entries.reason: Not in the shipped app: absent from the iOS and Android Metro source maps (see evidence). Build-time only: @expo/cli dev-server certificates and @expo/code-signing-certificates; app.json sets no updates code signing. No fixed release: the advisory covers <=1.4.0 and 1.4.0 (2026-03-24) is the newest node-forge. The 2026-10-04 lockfile moved 1.3.3 to 1.4.0, which cleared the other four node-forge advisories.

entries.title: PostCSS: Arbitrary file read and information disclosure via attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL in CSS comments
entries.reason: Not in the shipped app: absent from the iOS and Android Metro source maps (see evidence). Build-time only: @expo/metro-config's CSS transform; the app ships no CSS. No lockfile fix: every @expo/metro-config 54.0.x (pinned exactly by expo) requires postcss ~8.4.32, and 8.4.49, the newest 8.4.x, is affected; @expo/metro-config 57 moves to ^8.5.14. It leaves with an Expo SDK major.
